caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:ssc-7
attempts.paper_title: Layer 4 fast-spiking interneurons filter thalamocortical signals during active somatosensation
attempts.entry_title: Layer 4 fast-spiking interneurons filter thalamocortical signals (Yu et al. 2016)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings held up in this data. VPM and fast-spiking cells rose with whisking (VPM 4.3 to 11.9 spikes/s), their spikes were phase-locked to whisking, and cutting the infraorbital nerve removed fast-spiking touch and whisking responses. Thalamic photoinhibition lowered fast-spiking rates in direction, but the percentages differed from the paper's. Layer 4 excitatory cells did not show the reported lack of a whisking effect (p about 0.02), and the eNpHR touch-detection findings did not reproduce, although one of them flips with how passive first touches are handled. The inhibition seen at depolarized potentials, the thalamic multiunit photoinhibition and the rabies tracing could not be tested because those recordings are not in the dataset. Several latency and amplitude values were off, and the files do not say which tracked whisker is the principal one.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Yu, Gutnisky, Hires and Svoboda (2016) on CRCNS ssc-7, which holds spikes and membrane potential of VPM units, L4 excitatory neurons and L4 fast-spiking interneurons in mice localizing a pole with their whiskers, with whisker tracking, touch annotations, licks and optogenetic trials. It compares baseline, whisking and touch responses of the three cell types, the effects of infraorbital nerve transection, thalamic photoinhibition and PV interneuron suppression. The thalamic multiunit recordings, the rabies tracing and the recordings with depolarizing current injection are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Yu et al. (2016) from CRCNS ssc-7

outcomes.statement: Mice performed the task at 0.72 +- 0.11 correct during the cortical recordings (111 cells) and 0.71 +- 0.07 during the VPM recordings (29 cells); they touched the pole 5.7 +- 5.3 times per trial at a proximal location (4,147 trials) and 0.9 +- 3.4 times at a distal location (4,173 trials), and licked 286 +- 329 ms after the first touch.
outcomes.source: Online Methods, Behavior, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Mice touched the pole at a proximal location multiple times ... 5.7 ± 5.3, mean ± s.d., 4,147 trials) ... Average performance (proportion of correct trials) was 0.72 ± 0.11 (mean ± s.d., during the recordings of 111 cells) for cortical recordings and 0.71 ± 0.07 for VPM recordings
outcomes.notes: Under every combination of readings only cortical performance is within tolerance (0.706 over all good trials, 0.721 over control trials, n = 111 cells). VPM performance is 0.630 (n = 29). Touches per trial are 7.56 (Go, 7,097 trials) and 1.06 (Nogo, 6,872 trials) over the whole trial, 2.74 and 0.36 before the first lick. The reaction time is 328 to 340 ms. Proximal touches outnumber distal ones under every reading. With the principal whisker taken from the whisker configuration (variant), Go 5.93 and Nogo 0.63.
deviations: Touches are counted on the first tracked whisker series, taken as the principal whisker (an assumption; the files do not say which series is the principal whisker, see findings). The configuration-order reading is shown as a variant.

Proximal and distal trials are read as Go and Nogo trials (Online Methods, Behavior, "licked ... if the pole was in one of the posterior locations"). Trial counts pool the cortical recordings and each VPM session once; the paper's 4,147 and 4,173 trials cannot be matched to a set.
The data set's good-trial masks are applied.

outcomes.statement: VPM neurons fire at substantial rates in the absence of whisker movement and touch (5.1 +- 5.5 spikes/s, median 3.3, n = 29).
outcomes.source: Results, Chronic extracellular recordings from somatosensory thalamus, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Typical VPM neurons showed significant spike rates (mean ± s.d., 5.1 ± 5.5 spikes per s; median, 3.3 spikes per s; n = 29 neurons), even in the absence of whisker movement and touch
outcomes.notes: The nonwhisking mean is 4.34 to 4.82 spikes/s under the four readings (within 5.1 +- 1.02), the median 1.99 to 2.18 (outside 3.3 +- 0.33). Range 0.03 to 17.66 spikes/s. Seven units from one mouse (ANM199552) have a mean of 9.78.
deviations: Epoch rules follow M-EPOCH; whisking cycles run from one phase wrap to the next, and the margin readings (a) and (b) of the claims file are both shown.

outcomes.statement: VPM neurons respond to active touch with a sharp, short-latency, brief increase in spike rate (0.6 +- 0.5 spikes per touch, median 0.4; latency 3.2 +- 1.0 ms, median 2.5 ms; duration 2.9 +- 1.7 ms).
outcomes.source: Results, Chronic extracellular recordings from somatosensory thalamus, paragraphs 1 and 2; Fig. 1d; Supplementary Fig. 2
outcomes.quote: showed a sharp peak in spike rate (mean ± s.d., 0.6 ± 0.5 spikes per touch; median, 0.4 spikes per touch), with short latency after touch onset (mean ± s.d., 3.2 ± 1.0 ms; median, 2.5 ms) and brief duration (2.9 ± 1.7 ms, 25% of spike rate increase from baseline to peak
outcomes.notes: Spikes per touch 0.50 +- 0.43 (median 0.363, within tolerance; the mean is just outside). The latency is 2.48 ms on average and 1 ms median (n = 25 passing the exclusion; 13 units cross in the first 1 ms bin). Read at the bin centre, 2.98 ms (within) and median 1.5 ms (outside). The duration is 4.08 ms. The population PSTH peaks 2 ms after touch onset. The 1 ms difference in the median latency is not explained; the trial-type columns are Hit, Miss, CR, FA in the VPM files as in the cortical ones.
deviations: Latency on 1 ms PSTH bins; the latency is the first bin after the dPSTH/dt crossing. The duration follows the M-LAT reading of the claims file.
The first touch of trials tagged passive touch is left out, as the data set's example code compute_touchNWB.m does; its touch-speed cutoff is not applied.

outcomes.statement: Most VPM neurons (25 of 29) significantly increase their spike rate during whisking without touch; 3 of 29 do not increase but still respond to touch, and one decreases significantly.
outcomes.source: Results, Chronic extracellular recordings from somatosensory thalamus, paragraph 2; Fig. 1c,e; Supplementary Fig. 2
outcomes.quote: Most VPM neurons increased their spike rate during whisking in the absence of touch (25 out of 29 neurons ... A minority of VPM neurons (3 of 29) did not increase their spike rate with whisking but still responded to touch ... One neuron showed a significant decrease in spike rate during whisking (P < 0.0001)
outcomes.notes: Under M-SIG reading (b), per-trial rates, 24 increase, 1 decreases and 4 do not change, with either nonwhisking margin. Under reading (a), per-epoch rates, 22 or 21 increase and 6 or 7 do not change, outside tolerance. Whether the unchanged units respond to touch was not tested. The readings give different outcomes; the criterion accepts a match under one reading.
deviations: The readings of M-SIG give different counts; the criterion's rule of one matching reading decides.

outcomes.statement: The average VPM spike rate increases severalfold with whisker movement, from 5.1 +- 5.5 to 13.5 +- 12.7 spikes/s (n = 29, P = 4e-6, Wilcoxon signed-rank).
outcomes.source: Results, Chronic extracellular recordings from somatosensory thalamus, paragraph 2; Fig. 5d; Supplementary Fig. 2
outcomes.quote: The average spike rate increased severalfold after onset of whisker movement (from 5.1 ± 5.5 spikes per s to 13.5 ± 12.7 spikes per s; P = 4 × 10−6; n = 29 neurons, Wilcoxon signed-rank test

statistics.test: Wilcoxon signed-rank test

outcomes.notes: Nonwhisking 4.34 +- 4.79 and whisking 11.92 +- 11.67 spikes/s, ratio 2.74, signed-rank p = 5.2e-8, n = 29; all four sub-readings within tolerance. The onset variant gives 4.61 to 9.92 spikes/s (p = 3.7e-9).

outcomes.statement: VPM spike rate is modulated by the phase of whisker movement.
outcomes.source: Results, Chronic extracellular recordings from somatosensory thalamus, paragraph 2; Supplementary Fig. 2d to f
outcomes.quote: The spike rate was modulated by the phase of the movement (Supplementary Fig. 2d)
outcomes.notes: r2 > 0.25 in 27 of 29 units with 8 phase bins and 25 of 29 with 16. Coupling strength median 1.63 spikes/s (0.13 to 6.54), preferred phase median -0.38 rad. With spikes shuffled across whisking samples, 14 of 29 still pass the r2 cutoff, so the cutoff is weak.

outcomes.statement: Within a single behavioral session, VPM spike rate and whisking amplitude co-vary across trials (Pearson r = 0.61, P = 1e-78, 310 trials).
outcomes.source: Supplementary Fig. 1e
outcomes.quote: Spike rate and whisking amplitude co-vary across trials within single behavioral sessions (Pearson correlation coefficient ρ=0.61; P = 10-78; number of trials n=310)

statistics.test: Pearson correlation

outcomes.notes: No unit has a session of 310 good trials, so the criterion's fallback applies. 24 of 29 units show a significant positive Pearson r between trial rate and mean whisking amplitude. Three units have r within 0.61 +- 0.061 (3.3.33, 15.3.304, 11.2.110).
deviations: The trial rate and the amplitude are over the 5 s whisker video of each good trial.

outcomes.statement: The example L4 spiny stellate cell E No. 1 rests at -76 mV, far from its spike threshold (-45.1 +- 3.7 mV); touch evokes large (14.4 +- 8.2 mV), short-latency (4.7 ms), transient (24.5 ms at half max) depolarizations with 0 to 7 spikes per touch, while whisking without touch causes a smaller sustained depolarization (6.7 +- 4.0 mV) with little increase in spike rate (0.4 spikes/s).
outcomes.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 1; Fig. 2a to e
outcomes.quote: The neuron rested at a hyperpolarized potential (−76 mV) far from the spike threshold (mean ± s.d., −45.1 ± 3.7 mV). Active touch evoked large-amplitude (14.4 ± 8.2 mV), short-latency (4.7 ms) and transient (duration at half max, 24.5 ms) depolarizations that often triggered spikes (0–7 spikes per touch). In the absence of touch, whisking caused a sustained smaller depolarization (6.7 ± 4.0 mV)
outcomes.notes: JY0861, whose unit description names it neuron 1. All seven values are within tolerance under readings (a), and spikes per touch range from 0 to 7. The epoch reading of the whisking change gives 5.52 mV and the whisking-rate reading 0.55 spikes/s, both outside. The threshold s.d. over spikes is 8.91 mV against the paper's 3.7. With dVm/dt as a forward difference (variant), the threshold is -45.53 mV (within), s.d. 7.98 mV.
deviations: Spike thresholds are found by searching back from the data set's spike times for the dVm/dt crossing (Online Methods, Data analysis, paragraph 1); spikes are not detected again.

outcomes.statement: In the more depolarized example neurons, whisking causes a small depolarization (1.0 +- 1.4 mV, E No. 24) or a hyperpolarization (-1.8 +- 2.7 mV, E No. 32).
outcomes.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 1; Fig. 2d,e
outcomes.quote: For these neurons, whisking caused either small membrane potential depolarization (1.0 ± 1.4 mV, No. 24) or hyperpolarization (−1.8 ± 2.7 mV, No. 32)
outcomes.notes: With the onset measure and the 100 ms rise of M-EPOCH reading (b), E No. 24 (JY0520) +1.07 mV and E No. 32 (JY1008) -1.75 mV, both within tolerance. With the 250 ms rise, +1.29 (outside) and -1.65 (within); with the epoch measure +1.47 and -2.04, both outside. Both have the paper's sign under every reading. The criterion accepts one reading; the matching reading here is not the one that matches l4e-whisking-vm, so no single reading matches both claims.

outcomes.statement: The resting membrane potential of L4 excitatory neurons spans a large range, -76 to -45 mV (mean -63 +- 8 mV, median -64 mV, n = 37).
outcomes.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 2; Fig. 2f
outcomes.quote: Across the excitatory population, the resting membrane potential (Vm) spanned a large range (−76 to −45 mV, mean ± s.d., −63 ± 8 mV; median, −64 mV, n = 37 neurons
outcomes.notes: Range -76.0 to -44.3 mV, mean -62.7 +- 7.4, median -63.4 (reading a); reading (b) also within.

outcomes.statement: Touch evokes short-latency depolarizations in every L4 excitatory neuron (latency 4.8 +- 0.8 ms, median 4.7; amplitude 6.0 +- 2.9 mV, median 5.7; n = 37).
outcomes.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 2; Fig. 2f; Supplementary Fig. 3a
outcomes.quote: Touches evoked short-latency depolarizations ... mean ± s.d., 4.8 ± 0.8 ms; median, 4.7 ms ... mean ± s.d., 6.0 ± 2.9 mV; median, 5.7 mV; n = 37 neurons) for all neurons
outcomes.notes: All 37 amplitudes are positive. The latency median (5.0 ms) and the amplitude median (5.4 mV) are within tolerance. The latency mean (6.03 ms, n = 35) and the amplitude mean (5.26 mV) are not. Five latencies above 8 ms (9.5 to 22.1 ms) come from neurons with PSPs of 0.17 to 1.66 mV, against a median of 6.06 mV for latencies of 2.5 to 8 ms. Four latencies of 0.0 to 1.4 ms, shorter than the paper's VPM touch latency, are unlikely to be PSP onsets. Two neurons have no latency crossing. With the principal whisker taken from the whisker configuration, the amplitude is 4.18 mV (median 3.7) and only the latency median (4.8 ms) holds, so the outcome does not rest on that choice.

outcomes.statement: Whisking induces only a small depolarization or hyperpolarization in L4 excitatory neurons (1.2 +- 2.1 mV, median 1.2 mV).
outcomes.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 2; Fig. 2f
outcomes.quote: Whisking induced small depolarization or hyperpolarization (mean ± s.d., 1.2 ± 2.1 mV; median, 1.2 mV; Fig. 2f)
outcomes.notes: The onset reading gives 0.994 +- 2.03 mV, median 1.16 (n = 37), both within tolerance. The epoch reading gives 1.37 (median 1.35), and the 100 ms rise rule 0.677 (median 0.851), both outside. Vm after a later touch is set to NaN in the onset windows (M-EPOCH).

outcomes.statement: Touch moves the membrane potential of L4 excitatory neurons much closer to spike threshold than whisking does (shift 6.1 +- 3.2 mV against 1.1 +- 2.0 mV, P = 1e-7, Wilcoxon signed-rank).
outcomes.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 2; Fig. 2g,h
outcomes.quote: Compared to whisking, touch caused a larger shift of membrane potential toward spike threshold (whisking, 1.1 ± 2.0 mV; touch, 6.1 ± 3.2 mV; P = 1 × 10−7, Wilcoxon signed-rank test

statistics.test: Wilcoxon signed-rank test

outcomes.notes: Medians 0.87 mV (whisking) and 5.42 mV (touch); the signed-rank test gives p = 2.9e-11 under every reading. With the per-trial threshold line of M-VM, the touch mean (5.74 removed, 5.81 kept) is within tolerance and the whisking mean (-0.236 +- 5.89) is not. The largest whisking shift, -28.9 mV (JY0947), comes from a line through two thresholds in trials 126 and 129. With the line held at its end values outside the trials with spikes (variant), 0.767 and 5.34 mV, both outside. Only one mean threshold per neuron, not the paper's method, puts both within (0.784 and 5.52 mV, spikes kept). 11 neurons have no detected threshold and take the -42 mV default. The principal-whisker variant gives p = 6.1e-6.
deviations: Thresholds come from the data set's spike times (see l4e-example-e1). Where every threshold of a neuron falls in one trial, the per-trial line is not defined, and their mean is used; the first run fitted a line there. The line held at its end values outside the trials with spikes and one mean threshold per neuron are shown as variants.

outcomes.statement: The effective reversal potential of the touch response in L4 excitatory neurons is more depolarized than resting Vm, while that of the whisking response is close to resting Vm and more hyperpolarized than that of touch.
outcomes.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 2; Supplementary Fig. 4
outcomes.quote: The effective reversal potential29 of the touch response was more depolarized than the resting Vm and sometimes crossed the spike threshold (Supplementary Fig. 4). In contrast, the effective reversal potential for whisker movement was close to the resting Vm, below the spike threshold and more hyperpolarized than that for touch
outcomes.notes: Per neuron (n = 35), the touch reversal (median -49.8 mV) exceeds the whisking reversal (median -58.7), p = 2.6e-5, and lies above resting Vm in 34 of 35. The median whisking reversal is 4.9 mV above the median resting Vm (-63.4), inside the 5 mV margin, but close to it. Pooled, touch -45.4 and whisking -57.6 mV. One touch fit had a non-negative slope and was left out.
deviations: Vm after a later touch is set to NaN in the whisking-onset windows (M-EPOCH). The first run did not, and gave 5.6 mV, outside the margin.

outcomes.statement: Whisking enhances membrane potential fluctuations of L4 excitatory neurons at high frequencies (above 10 Hz).
outcomes.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 2; Supplementary Fig. 5
outcomes.quote: and enhanced membrane potential fluctuations at high frequencies (>10 Hz; Supplementary Fig. 5)
outcomes.notes: Over 36 neurons, whisking power exceeds nonwhisking power, 10 to 100 Hz (median ratio 1.17, p = 0.046), and 10 to 500 Hz (1.18, p = 0.030). 24 and 30 neurons have whisking power above the nonwhisking 95% bound over most of the band. The 10 to 100 Hz p is close to 0.05.
deviations: Multitaper spectra are computed in Python with three DPSS tapers (NW = 2), not with Chronux; 500 ms segments are taken from runs of consecutive whisking cycles.

outcomes.statement: In L4 excitatory neurons depolarized near the excitatory reversal potential, touch evokes strong transient inhibition that follows excitation with a short delay (0.4 +- 0.8 ms at half max, range -0.8 to 1.6 ms, n = 6).
outcomes.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 3; Fig. 3b to d; Discussion, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Touch elicited strong and transient inhibitory input (Fig. 3b,c), which followed excitation with a short delay (mean ± s.d., 0.4 ± 0.8 ms at half max; n = 6 neurons; Fig. 3d)
outcomes.notes: The six neurons recorded at rest and depolarized near 0 mV by current injection (Fig. 3) are not in the data set. Every ephys trial of every whole-cell file was read (the counts match the whisker trials). No L4 E trial has a median Vm above -42.8 mV and no L4 E current exceeds 0.2 nA, JY0978 (the cell list's Fig. 3 example) included. The only trials near 0 mV are the first 18 of the FS neuron JY1139, which keeps firing (8 to 85 spikes per trial) with no current above 0.1 nA, a drifting recording, not the protocol; JY1171 carries a steady current above 0.5 nA at -40.7 mV. No part of the claim can be tested.

outcomes.statement: Without touch, inhibitory input in L4 excitatory neurons is more prevalent at the onset of whisker movement, and after onset excitation and inhibition increase gradually with indistinguishable time courses over about 100 ms.
outcomes.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 3; Fig. 3e to g
outcomes.quote: In the absence of touch, inhibitory inputs occurred spontaneously but were more prevalent at onset of whisker movement (Fig. 3e,f) ... After the onset of whisker movement, excitation and inhibition increased gradually, with indistinguishable time courses, over approximately 100 ms (Fig. 3g)
outcomes.notes: Needs the depolarized recordings of Fig. 3, which are not in the data set (see l4e-inhibition-window); no part can be tested.

outcomes.statement: L4 FS interneurons are active at baseline, even without whisker movement (9.3 +- 8.5 spikes/s, median 6.4, n = 26).
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 1; Figs. 4b,c and 5
outcomes.quote: FS interneurons were active during baseline conditions, even in the absence of whisker movements (mean ± s.d., 9.3 ± 8.5 spikes per s; median, 6.4 spikes per s; n = 26 neurons
outcomes.notes: The 26 FS neurons of the two control FS folders give 9.43 +- 8.33 spikes/s, median 6.3; all four readings within tolerance.

outcomes.statement: Touch depolarizes L4 FS interneurons (7.0 +- 5.2 mV, median 6.7 mV, n = 7) with short onset latency (4.0 +- 0.6 ms, median 4.2 ms).
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 1; Fig. 4d,f
outcomes.quote: Membrane potential depolarized (mean ± s.d., 7.0 ± 5.2 mV; median, 6.7 mV; n = 7 neurons, Fig. 4d,f) ... Response latencies were short for membrane potential depolarization ... mean ± s.d., 4.0 ± 0.6 ms; median, 4.2 ms, n = 7 neurons
outcomes.notes: The seven whole-cell FS neurons give an amplitude of 6.8 +- 1.93 mV (median 6.97) and a latency of 3.67 +- 1.18 ms (median 3.9). With JY1139's drifting trials kept, 6.74, 6.97, 3.69 and 4.0, all within as well. With the principal whisker taken from the whisker configuration, which changes only JY1171, the latency mean is 7.24 ms (outside) and the other three values are within (6.23 mV, median 6.97 mV, latency median 3.9 ms), which would be partially reproduced.
deviations: The principal whisker is the first tracked series (assumption; see findings). The FS spike responses support it (1.78 against 0.45 spikes per touch); the configuration order is shown as a variant.

Trials whose median Vm lies more than 20 mV from the neuron's median are left out of the Vm measures: 13 trials of JY1139 (5 control trials), which starts near 0 mV and settles at about -41 mV. An assumption after the Methods' rejection of recordings "with slow baseline drift (>20 mV)" (Barrel cortex recordings, paragraph 3); keeping them is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: L4 FS interneurons fire about two spikes per touch (1.9 +- 1.0, median 1.9, n = 26) with short latency (5.3 +- 2.1 ms, median 4.5 ms, n = 24).
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 1; Fig. 5b,c
outcomes.quote: spike rates increased after touch (mean ± s.d., 1.9 ± 1.0 spikes per touch; median, 1.9 spikes per touch; n = 26 neurons ... and spiking (mean ± s.d., 5.3 ± 2.1 ms; median, 4.5 ms, n = 24 neurons; Fig. 5c)
outcomes.notes: Spikes per touch 1.83 +- 0.975 (median 1.95) and 25 neurons passing the latency exclusion are within tolerance. The latency mean 5.92 ms and median 4 ms are not. With the principal whisker taken from the whisker configuration, the FS neurons with two tracked whiskers give 0.45 spikes per touch on average, against 1.78 with the first series. Read at the bin centre, the latency median is 4.5 ms (within) and the mean 6.42 ms (outside), so three of five values hold at the bin edge and four at the bin centre.
deviations: The principal whisker is the first tracked series (assumption; see findings).

outcomes.statement: Most L4 FS neurons (23 of 26) significantly increase their spike rate during whisker movement without touch, and the rest (3 of 26) decrease it.
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: most L4 FS neurons significantly increased their spike rate during whisker movement without touch (23 of 26 neurons ... and a small subset (3 of 26 neurons, P ranged from 0.011 to 4.7 × 10−6) decreased spike rate
outcomes.notes: 21 or 22 increase and 3 decrease under all four readings.

outcomes.statement: After whisking onset the membrane potential of L4 FS neurons depolarizes toward spike threshold (2.7 +- 2.1 mV, median 2.4 mV, n = 7).
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 2; Fig. 4e to h
outcomes.quote: Overall, after onset of whisking, the membrane potential of FS neurons depolarized closer to spike threshold (mean ± s.d., 2.7 ± 2.1 mV; median, 2.4 mV, n = 7 neurons
outcomes.notes: The onset reading gives a mean of 2.02 mV (within 2.7 +- 0.79) and a median of 1.52 (outside 2.4 +- 0.24). The epoch reading gives 2.43, median 2.0, the 100 ms rise 1.54 (median 0.867), and the distance-to-threshold reading 0.976 (1.29 with one threshold per neuron). Under no reading is the median within tolerance, with or without JY1139's drifting trials.
deviations: Trials whose median Vm lies more than 20 mV from the neuron's median are left out of the Vm measures: 13 trials of JY1139 (5 control trials), which starts near 0 mV and settles at about -41 mV. An assumption after the Methods' rejection of recordings "with slow baseline drift (>20 mV)" (Barrel cortex recordings, paragraph 3); keeping them is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: With whisking the L4 FS spike rate doubles (to 21.1 +- 15.8 spikes/s, median 14.6, n = 26, P = 2.7e-5).
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 2; Fig. 5d
outcomes.quote: and the spike rate doubled (mean ± s.d., 21.1 ± 15.8 spikes per s; median, 14.6 spikes per s, n = 26 neurons, P = 2.7 × 10−5; Fig. 5d)

statistics.test: not named; paired comparison, Wilcoxon signed-rank by the Statistical analysis paragraph

outcomes.notes: Whisking 21.7 +- 16.3 (median 14.2) against 9.43 spikes/s, ratio 2.30, signed-rank p = 2.3e-5; all parts hold under all readings.

outcomes.statement: L4 FS spikes are coupled to whisking phase; the phase relation is fit by a single sinusoid in 18 neurons and needs a second harmonic in 7 (n = 25).
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 2; Supplementary Fig. 7g
outcomes.quote: Coupling between the spikes of L4 FS interneurons and the whisking phase was either fit with a single sinusoidal function (left, n=18) or a sum of a single sinusoidal function (black) and a sinusoidal function of twice the frequency (purple) (right, n=7) if the fitting quality (r2) was 50% higher than with only a single sinusoidal function
outcomes.notes: Coupling is present (single-sinusoid r2 > 0.25 in 25 of 26). The split is 22 single and 4 with a second harmonic (8 bins), or 21 and 5 (16 bins), against 18 and 7.
deviations: 26 neurons, where the Supplementary Fig. 7g legend gives 25.

outcomes.statement: In L4 FS interneurons, membrane potential fluctuations at high frequencies (above 10 Hz) increase with whisking in some cells but not in others (n = 7 whole-cell).
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 2; Supplementary Fig. 8
outcomes.quote: Membrane potential fluctuations increased at high frequencies (>10 Hz) for some cells but not others (Supplementary Fig. 8)
outcomes.notes: Whisking power lies above the nonwhisking 95% bound over most of the band in 6 of 7 neurons for both bands (5 and 6 with JY1139's drifting trials kept). Four neurons have 1 to 3 whisking segments. With nonwhisking segments split at random, a neuron passes the rule by chance with probability 0.02 to 0.22, about 1.0 and 0.7 of 7 neurons expected, so 6 of 7 is above chance.
deviations: Trials whose median Vm lies more than 20 mV from the neuron's median are left out of the Vm measures: 13 trials of JY1139 (5 control trials), which starts near 0 mV and settles at about -41 mV. An assumption after the Methods' rejection of recordings "with slow baseline drift (>20 mV)" (Barrel cortex recordings, paragraph 3); keeping them is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: L4 excitatory neurons respond mostly to touch (0.3 +- 0.4 spikes per touch, median 0.1, n = 85) and only weakly to whisker movement, with no significant change between nonwhisking (0.4 +- 0.6 spikes/s, median 0.1) and whisking (0.6 +- 0.9 spikes/s, median 0.2; P = 0.20).
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 3; Fig. 5b,d,e; Fig. 1f to j
outcomes.quote: Excitatory neurons responded mostly to touch (mean ± s.d., 0.3 ± 0.4 spikes per touch; median, 0.1 spikes per touch; n = 85 neurons; Fig. 5b,d) and showed weak response to whisker movement ... mean ± s.d., 0.4 ± 0.6 spikes per s; median, 0.1 spikes per s ... mean ± s.d., 0.6 ± 0.9 spikes per s; median, 0.2 spikes per s; n = 85, P = 0.20

statistics.test: not named; paired comparison, Wilcoxon signed-rank by the Statistical analysis paragraph

outcomes.notes: The claim of no whisking effect fails its test. The signed-rank test of whisking against nonwhisking rates gives p = 0.020 to 0.027 under all readings (mean difference 0.29 to 0.33 spikes/s, median 0). Spikes per touch are 0.20 (median 0.04) against 0.3 (0.1). The nonwhisking mean and the whisking median are within tolerance under every reading; the nonwhisking median is within under rate reading (a) (0.092) and outside under reading (b) (0.116 to 0.121). Whole-cell neurons give 0.096 spikes per touch, cell-attached ones 0.28. With the principal whisker taken from the whisker configuration, p = 0.0061 and spikes per touch 0.172, so the outcome does not rest on that choice.

outcomes.statement: Photoactivating TRN axons in VPM reduces thalamic activity to 17% of control (P = 3e-4, n = 17 multiunit recordings).
outcomes.source: Results, Inhibition is driven by thalamus, paragraph 1; Fig. 6b,c
outcomes.quote: Photoactivation of TRN axons reduced activity in the thalamus (to 17% of control, P = 3 × 10−4, n = 17 multiunit recordings

statistics.test: not named; paired comparison, Wilcoxon signed-rank by the Statistical analysis paragraph

outcomes.notes: The 17 thalamic multiunit recordings with patch pipettes during TRN-axon photostimulation are not in the data set; the only thalamic recordings are the 29 silicon-probe units, which have no photostimulation. The bucket listing and every member of data.tar.gz were checked.

outcomes.statement: Thalamic photoinhibition hyperpolarizes L4 excitatory neurons and reduces their Vm fluctuations, with an onset latency of 4.2 ms, longer than the 2.8 ms of direct cortical GABAergic activation.
outcomes.source: Results, Inhibition is driven by thalamus, paragraph 1; Supplementary Fig. 9b to f
outcomes.quote: photoinhibition of thalamus hyperpolarized excitatory neurons and reduced the amplitudes of their membrane voltage fluctuations (Supplementary Fig. 9a–e). Onset latency of Vm hyperpolarization induced by thalamus inactivation was 4.2 ms. This was longer than the 2.8-ms latency measured with direct cortical GABAergic activation
outcomes.notes: In the light period, Vm outside touch is lower in all 13 neurons (median -2.99 mV, p = 0.00024), and the 10 Hz high-passed variance falls to 0.59 of control (p = 0.00024). The rule as written crosses at the onset sample (0.0 ms), where dVm/dt is -295 and -392 mV/s. With 1 ms smoothing and a 1 ms hold, the thalamic latency is 4.8 ms (13 neurons) and the cortical one 2.6 ms (8 neurons). The thalamic latency is longer, and the cortical one is within tolerance. Over smoothing windows of 0.5 to 2 ms and holds of 0.5 to 2 ms, the thalamic latency is 4.5 to 5.0 ms and the cortical 2.0 to 2.7 ms; the thalamic one is always longer and no window puts both within tolerance.
deviations: The latency rule is read with 1 ms smoothing and a 1 ms hold, so that the step the light makes at the onset sample is not taken as the response. This is an assumption; the rule as written gives 0 ms for both.
Direct cortical activation trials are those with only the vS1 473 nm series on, in VGAT-ChR2 mice (8 neurons with an average; the paper has 7).
13 neurons, where the paper has 12.

outcomes.notes: The paper shows no data for these neurons ("data not shown"), and the ION-cut folders hold only L4 neurons (the cell list gives depths of 444 to 614 um for the ION-cut FS neurons).

outcomes.notes: Both means are within tolerance, but the mean change is significant (signed-rank p = 0.009; 0.027 over whole trials), and the correlation between control response and change is not (rho = -0.13, p = 0.42; whole trials -0.22, p = 0.16). One of the three parts holds.

outcomes.statement: PV interneuron suppression improves touch detection (AUC) for neurons with weak touch responses and diminishes it for neurons with robust touch responses.
outcomes.source: Results, Layer 4 FS interneurons suppress reafference in L4, paragraph 3; Fig. 8f,g
outcomes.quote: suppression of PV interneurons improved AUC for neurons with weak responses to touch and diminished AUC for neurons with robust responses to touch (Fig. 8f,g)
outcomes.notes: With the first touch of trials tagged passive left out, Spearman rho = -0.23, p = 0.16 (M-ROC reading a) and rho = -0.28, p = 0.09 (reading b), n = 37; the rank-sum variant gives p = 0.1 and 0.43. With those passive first touches kept, as in the first run, rho = -0.34, p = 0.038 under reading (b), so the outcome rests on the choice (143 trials tagged passive). Regression to the mean is small here: with control trials split in halves, the evoked rate of one half does not correlate with the AUC difference between halves (rho = 0.02, p = 0.91), and with rate and control AUC from different halves the claim's correlation is rho = -0.19, p = 0.27. Under reading (a) with the passive first touches kept, rho = -0.29, p = 0.086. Six neurons lack enough touch or no-touch trials. A question on the criterion is asked of a reader.
deviations: The AUC is computed over whole trials (the first touch, or a reference time, with 250 ms windows), as M-ROC describes; the light period is not applied.

The first touch of a trial tagged passive is not the trial's first touch; a trial whose only touch is that one is left out. An assumption: M-ROC says "the first touch", and the paper studies active touch, and the data set's compute_touchNWB.m leaves passive first touches out, as touch_table does for every other claim.

outcomes.statement: Of the 40 neurons, eNpHR stimulation increased AUC in 19 and reduced it in 21. Those with increased AUC raised their touch-evoked rates (3.4 +- 0.8 to 8.7 +- 1.9 spikes/s, P = 0.0001); those with reduced AUC kept their touch-evoked rates (7.3 +- 1.5 to 7.0 +- 1.4 spikes/s, P = 0.98) but raised their baseline rates (0.9 +- 0.2 to 2.6 +- 0.6 spikes/s, P = 0.0002).

Neurons with reduced AUC showed unchanged touchevoked responses as a population (from 7.3 ± 1.5 spikes per s to 7.0 ± 1.4 spikes per s, P = 0.98, average 0–250 ms after touch onset) ... but elevated baseline spike rates (from 0.9 ± 0.2 spikes per s to 2.6 ± 0.6 spikes per s, mean ± s.e.m., P = 0.0002

outcomes.notes: The AUC rose in 17 and fell in 20 neurons (reading a), or 24 and 13 (reading b). With raw rates and reading (a), the increased-AUC group's touch-evoked rate goes from 2.04 to 3.16 spikes/s (p = 0.04) and the reduced-AUC baseline rise (3.53 to 4.20) is not significant (p = 0.083); under reading (b) the increase is not significant (p = 0.069 to 0.084). At most one of six rates is within tolerance under any combination.

outcomes.statement: eNpHR stimulation strongly inhibits 3 of 4 recorded L4 PV interneurons; their spike rate falls 3 ms after laser onset and L4 excitatory activity rises only 2 ms later.
outcomes.source: Results, Layer 4 FS interneurons suppress reafference in L4, paragraph 6; Supplementary Fig. 13a,c
outcomes.quote: First, the spike rate of L4 PV interneurons decreased 3 ms after laser onset, and activity in L4 neurons increased only 2 ms later (Supplementary Fig. 13c)
outcomes.notes: Three of four PV neurons are strongly inhibited in the light period (rates at 0.05, 0.21 and 0.09 of control, rank-sum p < 1e-9); the fourth is unchanged (1.08, p = 0.64). On the sparse grand-average PSTH (1 ms bins), neither latency rule finds the PV decrease. The L4 E increase crosses at 17 ms (dPSTH/dt) or 7 ms (rate).
deviations: Strong inhibition is judged inside each trial's light period, by the criterion's rank-sum test and halving.

outcomes.statement: With PV interneurons suppressed most mice (6 of 8) are more likely to report touch with the pole out of reach; in an example session the false alarm rate rose from 20% to 61%.
outcomes.source: Results, Layer 4 FS interneurons suppress reafference in L4, paragraph 5; Supplementary Fig. 14b,c
outcomes.quote: Consistently, with PV interneuron suppressed, most mice (6 of 8) were more likely to report touches with the pole out of reach (Supplementary Fig. 14)
outcomes.notes: In the recording sessions of the 9 mice with eNpHR trials, 4 show a significant decrease in Nogo performance with light and none an increase, against 6 of 8 and 1. Leaving out any one mouse gives 3 or 4, so no 8 of the 9 match. No session matches the example (closest JY1247, false alarms 14% to 58%). Light falls in 23% to 48% of Nogo trials here, where the example describes "a small subset of trials". Per session the light share of Nogo trials is 14% to 70% (median 37%; 3 of 47 sessions under 20%). One mouse (ANM266951) has 7 Nogo trials and cannot give a significant result; without it, 8 mice give 4 decreases.
deviations: Tested on the recording sessions, assumed to be the sessions of Supplementary Fig. 14. The paper does not say which sessions it used, and the data set holds no other behavior with eNpHR light. Against the assumption: 9 mice here against 8, and no session matches the example. For it: the mouse with 7 Nogo trials may be the one the paper does not count, and some sessions have light in a small share of Nogo trials.

findings.statement: In the cortical files the whisker timestamps (processing/whisker/BehavioralTimeSeries/*/timestamps, labelled Seconds) are the trial start in milliseconds plus the time within the trial in seconds, so trial starts are 1,000 times those of the ephys timestamps. Read as milliseconds, each ephys trial starts 10 ms before the first whisker frame (10 kHz files) or with it (20 kHz files).

Seventy cortical files hold two tracked whisker series (whisker_angle_1, whisker_angle_2, with their touch annotations), and nothing says which whisker each is. Mapping them in the order of general/whisker_configuration to analysis/principal_whisker gives FS neurons almost no touch response (0.45 against 1.78 spikes per touch with series 1), while for several L4 E neurons it picks the series with the larger touch response (JY1345 0.857 against 0.235). The example code takes the first whisker as the main one.

Not in the data set, though the paper reports them. The 17 thalamic multiunit recordings during TRN-axon photostimulation (Fig. 6b,c), the rabies tracing (Supplementary Fig. 10), the L5 FS neurons after ION cut, and the whole-cell recordings with depolarizing current injection (Fig. 3, n = 6). No whole-cell L4 E trial has a median Vm above -42.8 mV.

The neuron JY1139 in the L4FS_whole_cell folder has the unit description "Excitatory", while the folder and the cell list's FS sheet give it as an FS neuron. Its first 18 trials have median Vm between -2.3 and -26.8 mV while it fires 8 to 85 spikes per trial with no injected current above 0.1 nA; from trial 20 it sits near -41 mV. Nothing in the file marks these trials.

Eight whole-cell L4 E files (JY0865, JY0861, JY1002, JY0989, JY0913, JY1009, JY0781, JY0986) flag 132 stimulus trials in analysis/trial_type_mat but hold no photostimulus series, and Exp_2015-09-24_004 and JY1633 have 23 flagged trials without light in their series. What stimulus these trials had cannot be read.

The eNpHR experiments hold 43 L4 E neurons with 594 nm light trials (39 cell-attached and 4 whole-cell), where the paper gives 40. Thalamic photoinhibition has 13 whole-cell L4 E neurons against 12, direct cortical activation 8 against 7, and the mice with eNpHR light number 9, where Supplementary Fig. 14 has 8.

For the authors. The onset latency of Vm after light onset (Supplementary Fig. 9c,f; 4.2 and 2.8 ms) is not defined in the paper. The touch rule (dVm/dt crossing 3 s.d. of its baseline) crosses at the onset sample, where the light makes a step in the average Vm. How was the light artifact handled, and was dVm/dt smoothed?

For the authors. Which tracked whisker series is the principal whisker in the files with two series, and was the touch-speed cutoff of compute_touchNWB.m (prct_speed 2.5) applied in the paper's analyses? Was the first touch of a trial tagged passive used as the trial's first touch in the ROC analysis of Fig. 8f,g? The correlation of enphr-auc is significant with it (p = 0.038) and not without it (p = 0.09).

The cell list (docs/yu_gutnisky_CellList.xlsx, sheet AllCellsReported) does not name JY1268, which the cell-attached L4 E folder holds with eNpHR light trials; its "Extracellular units" section has 47 rows against 48 files. It lists JY0781 among the PV-IRES-Cre L4 E neurons, though that file holds no photostimulus series.

entries.name: yu-2016-crcns-ssc-7
entries.title: Layer 4 fast-spiking interneurons filter thalamocortical signals (Yu et al. 2016)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Yu, Gutnisky, Hires and Svoboda (2016) on CRCNS ssc-7, which holds spikes and membrane potential of VPM units, L4 excitatory neurons and L4 fast-spiking interneurons in mice localizing a pole with their whiskers, with whisker tracking, touch annotations, licks and optogenetic trials. It compares baseline, whisking and touch responses of the three cell types, the effects of infraorbital nerve transection, thalamic photoinhibition and PV interneuron suppression. The thalamic multiunit recordings, the rabies tracing and the recordings with depolarizing current injection are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Yu et al. (2016) from CRCNS ssc-7
